description: Pluggable placement policy. The core measures (layout.geometry), asks the policy where to put the next pane, applies the decision, then measures again. The policy is a pure deterministic function tested with geometry fixtures; it never changes ownership or lifecycle and never closes a pane.

request.label: string
request.groupSize: optional integer: panes the caller's batch opens in all; absent when unknown

split.anchorKey: key of a live group pane

measuredSplit.rule: for every live group pane and each direction (right, down) compute both children from the measured rect at ratio 0.5; keep the candidate whose smaller child is largest, compared as the ratio to minCols for right and minRows for down; no candidate reaches the minimum, or the tab already holds maxPanesPerTab panes -> newTab
measuredSplit.tieBreak: smaller child score, then direction right before down, then the anchor that comes first in groupPanes order
measuredSplit.childSizes: right: floor(width*0.5) and width-floor(width*0.5); down: floor(height*0.5) and height-floor(height*0.5); measured on herdr: 352 -> 176+176, 69 -> 35+34

evenSplit.rule: n = panes the tab holds after this one, wanted = n plus what is left of the batch (groupSize minus live group panes, at least 1), capped at maxPanesPerTab; shape(count) = the most columns c <= count with area.width / c >= minCols, rows = ceil(count / c), refused when area.height / rows < minRows, columns = ceil(count / rows); the largest wanted down to n that has a shape sets the columns, none -> try the next tab of the group, then newTab
evenSplit.placement: fewer columns than the shape -> split the rightmost group pane right; otherwise split the largest group pane of the column that holds fewest panes down; a split whose children would fall under the minimum (whichever way herdr rounds) is skipped, and when nothing fits the policy answers newTab
evenSplit.ratio: groupSize absent: 0.5. groupSize present: 1/q where q is the number of panes the anchor's space must still hold (columns still missing plus one for a right split, the column's final pane count minus its current count plus one for a down split, at least 2), so the batch ends with equal panes; panes that join later are not rebalanced
evenSplit.measuredWidth: the shape reads the measured tab width per cell against minCols, never a screen ratio

noGeometry: when the driver lacks layout.geometry no policy runs: the core splits the newest live group pane down at 0.3 and opens a new tab at maxPanesPerTab panes
fixtures: policy-fixtures/*.json: {name, policy, input, expected}; policy names the registry entry the fixture is run against
